subtitle: Master the art of smooth chord connections and harmonic motion

backLink.label: Back to Chord Theory in Songs

introduction.title: The Flow Between Chords
introduction.text: Voice leading is how individual notes move from chord to chord. Good voice leading makes chord progressions sound smooth and connected rather than choppy and disconnected. It's the difference between beautiful, flowing harmony and awkward harmonic leaps.

columns.title: Independent Lines
columns.text: Each voice (soprano, alto, tenor, bass) has its own melodic line. Good voice leading creates 4 beautiful melodies happening simultaneously.

columns.title: Smooth Connection
columns.text: Minimize large leaps. When voices move smoothly (by steps or small intervals), the harmony flows naturally.

cards.title: Contrary Motion
cards.description: When one voice goes up, another goes down

fields.label: Example
fields.value: C to F: Bass C→F (up), Soprano G→A (up) - better if Soprano G→F (down)

cards.title: Smooth Voice Leading
cards.description: Move each voice by the smallest possible interval

fields.label: Example
fields.value: C to Am: C-E-G to A-E-G (only one note changes)

cards.title: Avoid Parallel 5ths/8ves
cards.description: Don't move voices in parallel perfect intervals

fields.label: Example
fields.value: C-G moving to D-A creates parallel 5ths (avoid this)

cards.title: Resolve Leading Tones
cards.description: Leading tone (7th scale degree) should resolve up to tonic

fields.label: Example
fields.value: In G7 to C: B should move to C

cards.title: Common Tones
cards.description: Keep common tones in the same voice when possible

fields.label: Example
fields.value: C to F: both have C - keep C in same voice

fields.label: Why It Works
fields.value: Three voices stay the same, only bass moves. Creates smooth, connected sound.

fields.label: Why It Works
fields.value: Leading tone resolves up, bass moves by 5th (strong), other voices move smoothly.

cards.title: IV - V (F to G)
cards.description: Smooth voice leading sets up dominant

badge.text: Smooth voice leading sets up dominant

fields.label: Why It Works
fields.value: Contrary motion between soprano and alto creates balance. Sets up strong V-I resolution.

cards.title: Piano/Keyboard
items: Practice chord progressions with close voicings (notes within an octave)
Focus on which fingers stay on the same keys between chords
Use voice leading to determine chord inversions
Practice scales in 4-part harmony to internalize smooth motion

cards.title: Guitar
items: Use chord inversions to create bass lines that connect smoothly
Practice moveable chord shapes that share common tones
Learn how to voice chords across different string sets
Focus on the top note (melody) of chord progressions

cards.title: Songwriting
items: Choose chord inversions based on the bass line you want
Consider the melody when selecting chord voicings
Use voice leading to create harmonic rhythm
Think about how chord tones connect to create secondary melodies

cards.title: Analyzing the Classic Progression: C - G - Am - F

fields.label: Top Voice (Melody) Movement
fields.value: C → B → A → A - Beautiful descending line that creates forward motion

fields.label: Bass Movement
fields.value: C → G → A → F - Strong root movement by 4ths and 5ths

items: Stepwise motion in the top voice (C→B→A)
Strong bass movement with clear harmonic direction
Inner voices move smoothly with minimal leaps
Common tones where possible (A held between Am and F)
Result: A progression that feels inevitable and emotionally satisfying

cards.title: What to Avoid
items: Parallel 5ths and octaves between voices
Large leaps when small steps would work
Unresolved leading tones
Crossing voices unnecessarily
Ignoring common tones between chords

cards.title: Best Practices
items: Move voices by the smallest possible distance
Keep common tones in the same voice
Use contrary motion when possible
Resolve tendency tones properly
Think melodically about each voice

exercises.title: Beginner Exercises
items: Practice I-V-I with smooth voice leading
Play chord progressions focusing on the top note
Identify common tones between adjacent chords
Practice the same progression with different chord inversions

exercises.title: Advanced Exercises
items: Compose 4-part harmony for simple melodies
Analyze voice leading in Bach chorales
Practice smooth voice leading with extended chords
Create bass lines that connect chord changes smoothly
